# Spec 2: Splitting a damage charge loses a cent

## Outcome

When a damage charge is shared between borrowers, every penny is billed to someone. The shares add up to the charge exactly, so charge D-301 (£33.33 between two borrowers) bills £16.67 and £16.66, not £16.66 twice.

## Requirements

- The system shall return shares from `splitCharge` that add up to exactly the charge, in integer cents.
- When a charge does not divide evenly, the system shall give one extra cent to each of the first (charge mod borrowers) borrowers, in order, so no two shares differ by more than one cent.
- If the charge is smaller than the number of borrowers, the system shall bill one cent each to the first borrowers and nothing to the rest.
- The system shall make `bun run desk split` print shares that add up to the charge, because it prints the shares `splitCharge` returns.

## Must not change

- Amounts stay integer cents; no floats.
- An even charge still splits into equal shares.
- One borrower still pays the whole charge.
- A negative charge, a non-integer charge, or fewer than one borrower is still refused with an error.
- Nothing under `src/auth/` is touched.

## Out of scope

- Weighted or unequal splits.
- Changing how the desk formats money.
- Fee rules other than damage-charge splitting (late fees, reservations, borrowing).

## Done when

- The new tests in `tests/fees/split.test.ts` pass and the existing tests still pass.
- `bun run gate` exits 0.

last_assistant_message:
I wrote the spec and three new tests, and all three fail on the current code. The other 10 tests still pass. I changed nothing under `src/`.

- **Spec:** `specs/2/SPEC.md` has the five required sections. The Requirements section has four one-line requirements:
  - The shares add up to the charge exactly.
  - Leftover cents go one each to the first borrowers, in order. D-301 would give £16.67 and £16.66.
  - A charge smaller than the number of borrowers bills one cent to each of the first borrowers and nothing to the rest.
  - `bun run desk split` prints shares that add up to the charge.
- **Tests:** I added them to `tests/fees/split.test.ts`, and the existing tests are untouched. One test covers the sums, one the leftover-cent order, and one the charge smaller than the number of borrowers. The failures are 3332 instead of 3333, `[1666, 1666]` instead of `[1667, 1666]`, and `[0, 0, 0]` instead of `[1, 1, 0]`.
- **Desk requirement:** the fourth requirement has no test of its own. `desk.ts` runs on import and needs a seeded database, so it would need a CLI test. It prints what `splitCharge` returns, so fixing `splitCharge` fixes the desk output.
- **Choice for you:** I chose to give the extra cents to the first borrowers in order, as the issue doesn't say who gets them. The rule is easy to change in the spec and tests if the library wants something else.
